title: difNLR
text: difNLR package provides methods detecting differential item functioning (DIF) using non-linear regression models. uniform non-uniform DIF effects can detected considering single focal group. Additionally, method allows testing differences guessing inattention parameters reference focal group. DIF detection performed using either likelihood-ratio test, F-test, Wald’s test submodel. software offers variety algorithms estimating item parameters. Furthermore, difNLR package includes methods detecting differential distractor functioning (DDF) using multinomial log-linear regression model. also introduces DIF detection approaches ordinal data via adjacent category logit cumulative logit regression models.

Possible values "" detecting difference parameter (default), "udif" uniform DIF (.e., difference difficulty parameter "b"), "nudif" non-uniform DIF (.e., difference discrimination parameter ""), "" uniform non-uniform DIF (.e., difference parameters "" "b"), combination parameters "", "b", "c", "d". Can specified single value (items) item-specific vector. method character: estimation method applied. options "nls" non-linear least squares (default), "mle" maximum likelihood method using "L-BFGS-B" algorithm constraints, "em" maximum likelihood estimation EM algorithm, "plf" maximum likelihood estimation algorithm based parametric link function, "irls" maximum likelihood estimation iteratively reweighted least squares algorithm (available "2PL" model ). See Details. match character numeric: matching criterion used estimate trait. can either "zscore" (default, standardized total score), "score" (total test score), numeric vector length number observations Data. anchor character numeric: specification DIF free items. vector item identifiers (integers specifying column number) specifying items currently considered anchor (DIF free) items. Argument ignored match "zscore" "score". start numeric: initial values estimation item parameters. specified, starting values calculated startNLR function. Otherwise, list many elements number items. element named numeric vector representing initial values estimation item parameters. Specifically, parameters "", "b", "c", "d" initial values discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention reference group. text: function calculates test statistics using DIF detection procedure based non-linear regression models (.e., extensions logistic regression procedure; Swaminathan & Rogers, 1990; Drabinova & Martinkova, 2017). unconstrained form 4PL generalized logistic regression model probability correct answer (.e., \(Y_{pi} = 1\)) using IRT parameterization $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(a_i + a_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) \cdot (X_p - b_p - b_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p))), $$ \(X_p\) matching criterion (e.g., standardized total score) \(G_p\) group membership variable respondent \(p\). Parameters \(a_i\), \(b_i\), \(c_{iR}\), \(d_{iR}\) discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention reference group item \(\). Terms \(a_{\text{DIF}}\) \(b_{\text{DIF}}\) represent differences focal reference groups discrimination difficulty item \(\). Terms \(c_{}\), \(d_{}\) guessing inattention parameters focal group item \(\). case assumed difference reference focal group guessing inattention parameters, terms \(c_i\) \(d_i\) used. Alternatively, intercept-slope parameterization may applied: $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(\beta_{i0} + \beta_{i1} \cdot X_p + \beta_{i2} \cdot G_p + \beta_{i3} \cdot X_p \cdot G_p))), $$ parameters \(\beta_{i0}, \beta_{i1}, \beta_{i2}, \beta_{i3}\) intercept, effect matching criterion, effect group membership, mutual interaction, respectively. model constraints arguments can constrain 4PL model. arguments model constraints can also combined. arguments can specified single value (items) item-specific vector (element corresponds one item). model argument offers several predefined models. options follows: Rasch 1PL model discrimination parameter fixed value 1 groups, 1PL 1PL model discrimination parameter set groups, 2PL logistic regression model, 3PLcg 3PL model fixed guessing groups, 3PLdg 3PL model fixed inattention groups, 3PLc (alternatively also 3PL) 3PL regression model guessing parameter, 3PLd 3PL model inattention parameter, 4PLcgdg 4PL model fixed guessing inattention parameter groups, 4PLcgd (alternatively also 4PLd) 4PL model fixed guessing groups, 4PLcdg (alternatively also 4PLc) 4PL model fixed inattention groups, 4PL 4PL model. function uses intercept-slope parameterization estimation via estimNLR function. Item parameters re-calculated IRT parameterization using delta method. function offers either non-linear least squares estimation via nls function (Drabinova & Martinkova, 2017; Hladka & Martinkova, 2020), maximum likelihood method "L-BFGS-B" algorithm constraints via optim function (Hladka & Martinkova, 2020), maximum likelihood method EM algorithm (Hladka, Martinkova, & Brabec, 2025), maximum likelihood method algorithm based parametric link function (Hladka, Martinkova, & Brabec, 2025), maximum likelihood method iteratively reweighted least squares algorithm via glm function.

text: Calculates DIF likelihood ratio statistics based either adjacent category logit model cumulative logit model ordinal data. Using adjacent category logit model, logarithm ratio probabilities two adjacent categories $$log(P(y = k) / P(y = k - 1)) = b_0k + b_1 * x + b_2k * g + b_3 * x:g,$$ \(x\) default standardized total score (also called Z-score) \(g\) group membership. Using cumulative logit model, probability gaining least \(k\) points given 2PL model, .e., $$P(y >= k) = exp(b_0k + b_1 * x + b_2k * g + b_3 * x:g) / (1 + exp(b_0k + b_1 * x + b_2k * g + b_3 * x:g)).$$ category probability (.e., probability gaining exactly \(k\) points) \(P(y = k) = P(y >= k) - P(y >= k + 1)\). models estimated iteratively reweighted least squares. details see vglm.

title: DIF detection using non-linear regression method. — difNLR
text: DIF detection procedure based non-linear regression extension logistic regression procedure (Swaminathan & Rogers, 1990) accounting possible guessing /inattention responding (Drabinova & Martinkova, 2017; Hladka & Martinkova, 2020). unconstrained form 4PL generalized logistic regression model probability correct answer (.e., \(Y_{pi} = 1\)) using IRT parameterization $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{} + c_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) + (d_{} + d_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p - c_{} - c_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) / (1 + \exp(-(a_i + a_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) \cdot (X_p - b_p - b_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p))), $$ \(X_p\) matching criterion (e.g., standardized total score) \(G_p\) group membership variable respondent \(p\). Parameters \(a_i\), \(b_i\), \(c_i\), \(d_i\) discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention reference group item \(\). Terms \(a_{\text{DIF}}\), \(b_{\text{DIF}}\), \(c_{\text{DIF}}\), \(d_{\text{DIF}}\) represent differences focal reference groups discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention item \(\), respectively. Alternatively, intercept-slope parameterization may applied: $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{} + c_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) + (d_{} + d_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p - c_{} - c_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) / (1 + \exp(-(\beta_{i0} + \beta_{i1} \cdot X_p + \beta_{i2} \cdot G_p + \beta_{i3} \cdot X_p \cdot G_p))), $$ parameters \(\beta_{i0}, \beta_{i1}, \beta_{i2}, \beta_{i3}\) intercept, effect matching criterion, effect group membership, mutual interaction, respectively. model constraints arguments can constrain 4PL model. arguments model constraints can also combined. arguments can specified single value (items) item-specific vector (element corresponds one item). model argument offers several predefined models. options follows: Rasch 1PL model discrimination parameter fixed value 1 groups, 1PL 1PL model discrimination parameter set groups, 2PL logistic regression model, 3PLcg 3PL model fixed guessing groups, 3PLdg 3PL model fixed inattention groups, 3PLc (alternatively also 3PL) 3PL regression model guessing parameter, 3PLd 3PL model inattention parameter, 4PLcgdg 4PL model fixed guessing inattention parameter groups, 4PLcgd (alternatively also 4PLd) 4PL model fixed guessing groups, 4PLcdg (alternatively also 4PLc) 4PL model fixed inattention groups, 4PL 4PL model. underlying generalized logistic regression model can specified detail constraints argument specifies parameters fixed groups. example, choice "ad" means discrimination (parameter "") inattention (parameter "d") fixed (estimated ) groups parameters ("b" "c") . text: Calculates DIF likelihood ratio statistics based either adjacent category logit model cumulative logit model ordinal data. Using adjacent category logit model, logarithm ratio probabilities two adjacent categories $$log(P(y = k) / P(y = k - 1)) = b_0k + b_1 * x + b_2k * g + b_3 * x:g,$$ \(x\) default standardized total score (also called Z-score) \(g\) group membership. title: Creates a formula for non-linear regression DIF models. — formulaNLR
text: unconstrained form 4PL generalized logistic regression model probability correct answer (.e., \(Y_{pi} = 1\)) using IRT parameterization $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(a_i + a_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) \cdot (X_p - b_p - b_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p))), $$ \(X_p\) matching criterion (e.g., standardized total score) \(G_p\) group membership variable respondent \(p\). Parameters \(a_i\), \(b_i\), \(c_{iR}\), \(d_{iR}\) discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention reference group item \(\). Terms \(a_{\text{DIF}}\) \(b_{\text{DIF}}\) represent differences focal reference groups discrimination difficulty item \(\). Terms \(c_{}\), \(d_{}\) guessing inattention parameters focal group item \(\). case assumed difference reference focal group guessing inattention parameters, terms \(c_i\) \(d_i\) used. Alternatively, intercept-slope parameterization may applied: $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(\beta_{i0} + \beta_{i1} \cdot X_p + \beta_{i2} \cdot G_p + \beta_{i3} \cdot X_p \cdot G_p))), $$ parameters \(\beta_{i0}, \beta_{i1}, \beta_{i2}, \beta_{i3}\) intercept, effect matching criterion, effect group membership, mutual interaction, respectively. model argument offers several predefined models. options follows: Rasch 1PL model discrimination parameter fixed value 1 groups, 1PL 1PL model discrimination parameter set groups, 2PL logistic regression model, 3PLcg 3PL model fixed guessing groups, 3PLdg 3PL model fixed inattention groups, 3PLc (alternatively also 3PL) 3PL regression model guessing parameter, 3PLd 3PL model inattention parameter, 4PLcgdg 4PL model fixed guessing inattention parameter groups, 4PLcgd (alternatively also 4PLd) 4PL model fixed guessing groups, 4PLcdg (alternatively also 4PLc) 4PL model fixed inattention groups, 4PL 4PL model. Three possible parameterizations can specified "parameterization" argument: "irt" returns IRT parameters reference group differences parameters reference focal group. Parameters asymptotes printed separately reference focal groups. "" returns intercept-slope parameterization. Parameters asymptotes printed separately reference focal groups. "logistic" returns parameters logistic regression parameterization glm function, available 2PL model.

title: Calculates starting values for non-linear regression DIF models. — startNLR
text: unconstrained form 4PL generalized logistic regression model probability correct answer (.e., \(Y_{pi} = 1\)) using IRT parameterization $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(a_i + a_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p) \cdot (X_p - b_p - b_{\text{DIF}} \cdot G_p))), $$ \(X_p\) matching criterion (e.g., standardized total score) \(G_p\) group membership variable respondent \(p\). Parameters \(a_i\), \(b_i\), \(c_{iR}\), \(d_{iR}\) discrimination, difficulty, guessing, inattention reference group item \(\). Terms \(a_{\text{DIF}}\) \(b_{\text{DIF}}\) represent differences focal reference groups discrimination difficulty item \(\). Terms \(c_{}\), \(d_{}\) guessing inattention parameters focal group item \(\). case assumed difference reference focal group guessing inattention parameters, terms \(c_i\) \(d_i\) used. Alternatively, intercept-slope parameterization may applied: $$P(Y_{pi} = 1|X_p, G_p) = (c_{iR} \cdot G_p + c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) + (d_{iR} \cdot G_p + d_{} \cdot (1 - G_p) - c_{iR} \cdot G_p - c_{} \cdot (1 - G_p)) / (1 + \exp(-(\beta_{i0} + \beta_{i1} \cdot X_p + \beta_{i2} \cdot G_p + \beta_{i3} \cdot X_p \cdot G_p))), $$ parameters \(\beta_{i0}, \beta_{i1}, \beta_{i2}, \beta_{i3}\) intercept, effect matching criterion, effect group membership, mutual interaction, respectively. model argument offers several predefined models. options follows: Rasch 1PL model discrimination parameter fixed value 1 groups, 1PL 1PL model discrimination parameter set groups, 2PL logistic regression model, 3PLcg 3PL model fixed guessing groups, 3PLdg 3PL model fixed inattention groups, 3PLc (alternatively also 3PL) 3PL regression model guessing parameter, 3PLd 3PL model inattention parameter, 4PLcgdg 4PL model fixed guessing inattention parameter groups, 4PLcgd (alternatively also 4PLd) 4PL model fixed guessing groups, 4PLcdg (alternatively also 4PLc) 4PL model fixed inattention groups, 4PL 4PL model. Three possible parameterizations can specified "parameterization" argument: "irt" returns IRT parameters reference group differences parameters reference focal group. Parameters asymptotes printed separately reference focal groups. "" returns intercept-slope parameterization. Parameters asymptotes printed separately reference focal groups. "logistic" returns parameters logistic regression parameterization glm function, available 2PL model.
